Dozens of soldiers, militants and miners killed in Nigeria attacks

Reuters

07 October, 2026 11:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Ahmed Kingimi MAIDUGURI, Nigeria, Oct 7 (Reuters) – Nigerian troops killed more than 25 Islamic State-aligned militants as they fought off an assault on a military position in northeastern Borno State, suffering an unknown number of casualties of their own, military sources and a member of the civilian defence force said on Wednesday.

In a separate, earlier incident, gunmen on motorbikes killed more than 25 soldiers and over 100 small-scale gold miners in Zamfara State, in the northwest, a military source, government official, and three residents said.

The attacks underscore the persistent threat posed by Islamist insurgents in northeastern Nigeria despite years of military campaigns against Boko Haram and its offshoot, known as Islamic State West Africa Province. Meanwhile, violence is spreading in the northwest, where bandits and Islamist groups also operate.

Show Full Article

Insecurity is likely to be a key issue in Nigeria’s election early next year.

SPECIAL FORCES UNDER ATTACK

In the incident in the northeast, troops of the 101 Special Forces Battalion came under attack on Tuesday night from four directions in Kukawa, near Lake Chad, but repelled the assault with air support, according to the military.

“Preliminary assessment indicates that over 25 terrorists were neutralised, with 14 bodies recovered so far,” Captain Mohammed Goni, acting military information officer for Operation Hadin Kai, said in a statement. Troops seized six AK-47 rifles and ammunition during follow-up operations.

The military sources said some soldiers were killed in the fighting but did not provide details.

A member of the Civilian Joint Task Force, which supports military operations in the northeast, said more than three of its members were killed.

The military said it would continue joint operations to prevent militants from regrouping and launching further attacks.

GUNMEN ON MOTORBIKES

On October 5, heavily armed bandits on motorcycles attacked a military camp in Bindin, a community in Zamfara’s Maru local government area, killing at least 25 troops, three eyewitnesses told Reuters.

Salisu Abdu, a resident of the nearby Bindin village, said he had counted the bodies of 25 dead soldiers.

A military source who participated in an operation to reinforce security in the community on Wednesday confirmed the attack, saying that he too saw 25 bodies. The gunmen looted the base after overrunning the soldiers, he said.

The gunmen then opened fire in a mining pit on Tuesday where about 1,000 people were digging for gold.

At least 100 people were killed, according to a village head and relatives of the victims.

Reuters could not confirm the casualty figures. Neither the Nigerian military nor the Zamfara State government responded to requests for comment.

(Writing by Chijioke Ohuocha and Ben Ezeamalu, Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria, David Lewis and Bill Berkrot)

Rubio, in Athens, ties ancient values to ‘America First’

Reuters

07 October, 2026 11:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Jonathan Landay ATHENS, Oct 7 (Reuters) – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday urged Western nations to embrace the ancient Greek values of “heroism, honor, and duty”, tying the ideals to President Donald Trump’s “America First” agenda.

“It’s become fashionable today to believe that enlightened foreign policy means prioritizing the global community over one’s own people,” Rubio told Greek officials, diplomats and other invitees.

With the ruins of the Parthenon in the distance behind him, he said the men of ancient Greece “knew that there was nothing selfish or wrong about loyalty to your nation.”

Show Full Article

Rubio, a potential contender for the Republican nomination to succeed Trump in 2028, delivered the speech from the Pnyx, where ancient Athens’ popular assembly once met.

Rubio’s speech echoed Vice President JD Vance’s February 2025 Munich Security Conference speech, which cast Europe’s challenges as a retreat from shared Western values and drew rebukes from the continent’s leaders.

That was followed by Trump’s November 2025 National Security Strategy, which warned that Europe faced “civilization erasure” from migration and challenges to national sovereignty.

“Today, we find ourselves at a crossroads, because the next decade and the decisions we make will write the story of the next century,” Rubio said. “The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world, or resigns itself to a future of atrophy, and servitude, and decline.”

“Under President Trump, the United States has made its choice,” Rubio added. “We choose the unapologetic pursuit of national power.”

Rubio is visiting three European NATO allies as part of a trip that began in Iceland. Earlier on Wednesday, Rubio and his Greek counterpart reaffirmed close US-Greek security, energy and trade ties. He concludes the trip with talks with Portuguese officials on Thursday in Lisbon.

(Reporting by Jonathan Landay in Athens; Additional reporting by Simon Lewis in Washington; Editing by Alison Williams and Deepa Babington)

Exclusive-Lebanon’s Hezbollah gets $200 million from Iran to help displaced, sources say

Reuters

07 October, 2026 11:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Laila Bassam and Maya Gebeily BEIRUT, Oct 7 (Reuters) – Hezbollah has received $200 million from Iran to help Lebanese displaced by this year’s war with Israel, two people with direct knowledge of the transfer said, in what would be the first significant aid from the group to supporters who bore the brunt of the conflict.

The US disputed the claim. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement that the money “is not there,” accusing Hezbollah of “trying to save face with fake stories about cash influxes from Iran.”

Hezbollah received the cash last month despite a tightening US economic chokehold on Iran and increasing difficulties in getting funds to Tehran’s Lebanese ally, said the people.

Show Full Article

Intermediaries who moved the money charged a 20% fee, reflecting the risks of dealing with the group, they said. One said this was four times the normal fee.

Asked for comment, a Hezbollah official said an amount had been secured and a plan for distributing it would be announced in the coming days, without elaborating on the source of the funds.

The Iranian foreign ministry, Iran’s permanent mission in Geneva, and the Lebanese government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Israel’s bombardment and invasion of Lebanon uprooted hundreds of thousands of Hezbollah’s Shi’ite Muslim constituents after the group entered the regional war in support of Iran on March 2.

But those displaced have so far received little to no assistance from Hezbollah, an armed group founded by Iran’s Revolutionary Guards in 1982 which has suffered heavy Israeli blows in two wars since 2024 and is designated a terrorist group by Washington.

The State Department’s Pigott said Hezbollah had caused misery for Lebanese and had itself been decimated, while its backer Tehran was suffering under a US blockade of oil exports. “The United States will continue to strangle Hizballah’s finances through sanctions while supporting the ability of Lebanon’s legitimate government to rebuild the South,” Pigott said.

AIDING 50,000 FAMILIES

Hezbollah would use the funds to pay an initial $3,000 per family, and priority will go to those whose villages have been destroyed or are inaccessible due to Israeli occupation, the sources said. These number around 50,000 families, one of the sources said.

Iran has maintained financial support to Hezbollah through years of crippling US sanctions: it transferred $1 billion to the group in the first 10 months of 2025, according to the US Treasury Department.

Tehran has never acknowledged financing Hezbollah. Iran’s policy of funding regional proxies has stirred domestic protester anger against the clerical rulers in the past and could prove particularly sensitive at a time of worsening hardship in Iran.

Iran had promised Hezbollah more funding after Tehran signed an interim deal with Washington in June that allowed Iran to sell its oil, Reuters reported at the time. That agreement collapsed in July.

Washington has since intensified economic pressure on Iran, tightening sanctions and imposing a naval blockade to block Iranian oil exports.

Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem said in a speech last month that the group would soon contribute to a project aimed at housing thousands of people displaced by the war, using “available resources and donations”, without elaborating.

Hezbollah’s ability to fund local services and provide post-conflict aid has helped shore up its support in the past. Following a war with Israel in 2006, the group immediately handed out large cash payments to those impacted and moved swiftly to help rebuild Beirut’s southern suburbs, a stronghold.

But this time there has been little sign of reconstruction. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said last month that the total reconstruction costs from the two wars since 2024 could exceed $27 billion.

A COSTLY WAR

The two sources provided no details on how the money got to Lebanon.

One of them said it was increasingly difficult for Hezbollah to move funds via financial companies that once processed such transfers. Such firms based in Iraq and Dubai were no longer an option, and they were also now under pressure in Turkey, this source said.

Hezbollah’s foes believed money was currently the group’s “oxygen”, the source added. Despite the difficulties securing funding, the group had not stopped paying its fighters and the family members of those killed in combat, this source said.

In Lebanon, the war has inflicted a heavy price on the Shi’ite Muslim community from which Hezbollah draws support. Israel has razed villages across a swathe of territory it has seized in the south, saying it aims to shield northern Israel from Hezbollah attack.

Israeli attacks in Lebanon have killed more than 4,300 people since March 2, according to Lebanon’s health ministry. Its toll does not say how many combatants may be among the dead. Hezbollah has not disclosed figures on its war dead. Reuters reported on May 4 that several thousand Hezbollah fighters had been killed in the war.

(Additional reporting by Simon Lewis; Writing by Tom Perry; Editing by Peter Graff and Nick Zieminski)

Germany’s AfD calls for end to support for Ukraine

Reuters

07 October, 2026 10:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

BERLIN, Oct 7 (Reuters) – Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) will launch a joint motion with the small far-left BSW party in a regional parliament calling for an end to military support for Ukraine, an AfD spokesperson said on Wednesday.

The motion, to be debated in the state parliament of Saxony-Anhalt next week, will have no immediate impact on Germany’s foreign policy, which is exclusively the responsibility of the federal government in Berlin.

But it underscores the AfD’s strong push for an end to German support for Ukraine and a restoration of ties with Russia, which have been largely severed since Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Show Full Article

“This motion symbolises the desire for change,” Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD leader in Saxony-Anhalt, said in a statement.

Siegmund led the anti-immigration AfD to its best-ever election result last month, topping the state election in Saxony-Anhalt but falling just short of the majority he would need to form the first-ever AfD government.

He has since been exploring potential cooperation arrangements with the BSW, which like the AfD has long opposed German support for Ukraine.

Siegmund said the party would use every opportunity to press the government of Chancellor Friedrich Merz “to finally campaign for an end to the war rather than its prolongation” and to use the money spent in Ukraine “for the people in our country”.

In a message on the social media platform X, BSW founder Sahra Wagenknecht said Germany needed “a federal government that finally makes an effort to resume dialogue with Moscow”.

The motion comes some two weeks after German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul spoke to his Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York at a meeting that yielded no sign of any progress.

Lavrov was dismissive about the meeting in a press conference afterwards. Germany’s Foreign Ministry said the meeting had reinforced Berlin’s conviction that Moscow remains unwilling to negotiate either a ceasefire or an end to the war in Ukraine.

Merz visited Kyiv at the weekend to reaffirm Berlin’s support for Ukraine, while German authorities have accused Russia of carrying out a series of hybrid and drone attacks in Germany, something that Moscow denies.

(Reporting by James MackenzieEditing by Gareth Jones)
